In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ice phobic coating of line conductors is a more effective measure to increase system resilience against snow storms, as compared to the redispatching of thermal power plants.
the ice phobic conductors are the most suitable measure for mitigating the effects of wet snow storms on power systems.
the ice phobic coating of line conductors, in combination with a proper preventive redispatching, can be a valid strategy to increase the system resilience against wet snow storms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the paper provides a methodology to assess the system response to natural threats and to identify suitable countermeasures for increasing the system resilience, by accounting for the different sensitivities of the system to the threat intensities and to the countermeasures effectiveness.

, by using the proposed methodology, the system operators can assess the impact of extreme weather events on power systems, by taking into account the system response under the different mitigation measures.
, by means of a proper sensitivity analysis, it is possible to identify the critical contingencies, to quantify the system resilience and to evaluate the effectiveness of the countermeasures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the resilience analysis is a powerful tool to support decision makers in the planning of preventive and corrective countermeasures.
the proposed methodology can be easily adapted to different threats and to different power systems.
a model based resilience assessment is a useful tool for the TSOs to identify the most critical contingencies and to assess the effectiveness of countermeasures.
